title: Amid Middle East, Red Sea disruptions: Colombo Free Zone offers safe cargo routing
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Amid the ongoing instability in the Middle East and the Red Sea region, Colombo’s Free Zone operations have been positioned as a secure alternative routing solution for global cargo movements. With shipping lines and airlines facing operational disruptions and heightened security risks in affected zones, logistics operators in Colombo are offering contingency routing options to ensure continuity of trade and delivery commitments. The Colombo Free Zone is facilitating multiple routing combinations, including sea-to-sea (SEA/SEA), sea-to-air (SEA to AIR), air-to-sea (AIR to SEA), and air-to-air (AIR/AIR) transfers. The scope of services includes cross-stuffing, palletising, re-documentation, short-term storage, and onward booking — all conducted under Free Zone status, ensuring there is no duty impact on cargo in transit. Industry sources said the alternative routing mechanism enables shippers to bypass high-risk maritime and air corridors while effectively managing transit delays caused by the regional crisis. Logistics stakeholders noted that the initiative aims to provide immediate, flexible solutions for shipments requiring contingency arrangements, positioning Colombo as a reliable transshipment and redistribution hub during the ongoing geopolitical uncertainty.

title: Substandard medicine racket: MCPA demands extradition of key suspect
summary: By Khalidha Naushad Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa, President of the Medical and Civil Rights Professional Association of Doctors (MCPA), has raised concerns about the Criminal Investigation Department’s (CID) failure to extradite a Health Ministry doctor who allegedly fled the country two years ago in connection with a substandard medicine racket. Dr. Jayanath Buthpitiya, who served in the Ministry of Health at the time, is considered a key suspect in the case currently before the courts. Despite a Red Notice being issued against him, he remains at large. “It is highly questionable why the doctor involved in the substandard medicine racket, who fled the country, remains in hiding,” Dr. Sanjeewa stated. According to Dr. Sanjeewa, the suspect is believed to possess vital secrets regarding the regulation and procurement of medicine supplies within the Ministry of Health between 2019 and 2024. He claims the CID’s failure to bring him back has hindered the discovery of extensive information regarding what he describes as the “medicinal drug mafia and rackets” that existed within the health system. Dr. Sanjeewa said Dr. Buthpitiya’s presence would strengthen the prosecution of the ongoing case involving the former Health Minister and 13 other officials. “It is imperative to extradite the doctor immediately, as there is strong suspicion that he holds specific information regarding questionable transactions that occurred during the Covid-19 pandemic within units such as the Medical Supplies Division, the National Medicines Regulatory Authority, and the Medical Research Institute,” Dr. Sanjeewa stated. The CID has not publicly commented on the status of extradition efforts or the challenges faced in securing Dr. Buthpitiya’s return.

title: Middle East conflict threatens regional stability – Sajith
summary: By Naalir Jamaldeen Leader of the Opposition and Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) Sajith Premadasa has claimed that the escalating aggression and widening conflict across the Middle East pose a grave threat to regional stability and global peace due to the ongoing war between the USA–Israel alliance and Iran. Taking to X, Opposition Leader Premadasa stated that any expansion of hostilities—whether through attacks or destabilising actions targeting countries such as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, or other nations in the region—must be unequivocally condemned. He added that the human cost of war is always the heaviest burden. Millions of civilians across the region face insecurity, displacement, and economic hardship. In particular, the safety and well-being of over one million Sri Lankans working in the Middle East remain a matter of profound concern. Their livelihoods support families back home and contribute significantly to Sri Lanka’s economy. Any further escalation would put innocent lives and vital economic stability at serious risk. Premadasa stressed that war rarely delivers lasting solutions. Dialogue, diplomacy, and negotiated settlements remain the only sustainable path forward. Immediate efforts towards ceasefire agreements, peace talks, and constructive negotiations are essential to prevent further suffering and regional destabilisation. He emphasised that the international community must act responsibly and urgently to prevent further military escalation, protect civilian populations and migrant workers, safeguard critical infrastructure and economic stability, and facilitate inclusive and credible peace negotiations. History has repeatedly shown that conflicts left unchecked grow more complex and destructive. The time to act for peace is now. War must be avoided at all costs. The protection of human life, regional stability, and global security demands restraint, courage, and a renewed commitment to diplomacy.

title: To prevent potential shortage: Govt must prepare alternative fuel plans – Attanayake
summary: By Naalir Jamaldeen Tissa Attanayake, National Organiser of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), yesterday (3), urged the Government to prepare alternative plans to meet the country’s fuel demand once the current one-month stock runs out. Addressing the media in Colombo, Attanayake said that while the Government has assured the public of sufficient fuel stocks for a month, it must also be ready to prevent a potential shortage once those reserves are depleted. He noted that if adequate fuel stocks are available, the public need not panic. However, he cautioned that relying on imports from countries such as India and Singapore may not be a secure long-term solution, particularly if the ongoing conflict in the Middle East escalates and disrupts global fuel supplies. He stressed that the Government must prioritise the safety and well-being of Sri Lankans employed in Middle Eastern countries. He highlighted several urgent matters requiring immediate attention, including protecting the lives and employment of Sri Lankan migrant workers in the Middle East, safeguarding foreign remittances sent by these workers, and ensuring the stability of tea exports, noting that nearly 25% of Sri Lanka’s tea exports are destined for Middle Eastern markets. title: Citing ‘serious safety risks’: U.S. citizens told to leave 14 Middle Eastern countries
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan The United States’ Department of State has urged Americans to immediately depart several countries in the Middle East using available commercial transportation, citing “serious safety risks” amid escalating tensions in the region. In a security update issued on 2 March, the department called on US citizens in affected areas to leave without delay and to make use of commercial travel options while they remain available. The advisory applies to Americans in Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, including the West Bank and Gaza, as well as Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. “Depart now via commercial means due to serious safety risks,” the notice stated. Americans requiring assistance in arranging their departure have been advised to contact the State Department’s 24-hour helplines (from the United States and Canada). The US citizens were also encouraged to enrol in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Programme (STEP) to receive the latest security updates from the nearest US embassy or consulate.

title: Following enactment of Inland Revenue Bill: TIN to become mandatory for many services
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Following the enactment of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Bill, which has already been gazetted, a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) certificate will become mandatory for a range of services. Accordingly, individuals will be required to present a TIN certificate when opening an account at any financial institution, obtaining approval for a building plan, registering a motor vehicle or renewing a vehicle licence, registering land or land ownership, registering a business, transferring shares of a company incorporated in Sri Lanka by a transferee, and obtaining credit cards. The new requirement is expected to come into effect from April.

title: GL urges Govt to address Middle East fallout
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Former Foreign Minister Prof. G.L. Peiris has written to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, warning that the ongoing crisis in the Middle East could have serious and immediate repercussions for Sri Lanka. Writing on behalf of concerned citizens, Prof. Peiris stressed the need for the Government to promptly communicate its position to both the public and the international community. The letter further noted that the crisis affects Sri Lanka in at least four key areas. First, escalating global oil prices are expected to drive up local fuel costs, significantly increasing the cost of living and aggravating the economic hardships already faced by the public. Second, export revenues, particularly from commodities such as tea, may decline due to restricted access to key markets affected by active military conflicts in the region. Third, the tourism and hotel sector is already experiencing considerable cancellations from prospective tourists from Europe, North America, and the Gulf, who face difficulties related to air travel across the affected regions. Fourth, the situation threatens the viability of remittances from Sri Lankan workers throughout the Gulf and wider areas, which are a critical source of foreign income for the country. Prof. Peiris stressed that citizens are prepared to assist the Government in addressing these multifaceted challenges and are actively discussing practical measures to mitigate the crisis’s effects. A public briefing is planned in the near future to share these discussions and proposals. He also urged the Government to release basic information on its approach to the crisis. This, he said, would allow the public to participate in an informed manner and help ensure transparency in navigating these troubling developments.

title: How to Lead Without a Title: Influencing From Within
summary: By Prasanna Perera Leadership is often mistakenly associated with titles, corner offices, or positions of authority. However, in today’s dynamic work environments, true leadership exceeds these traditional markers. It lies in the ability to inspire, influence, and drive meaningful change, regardless of one’s official position within an organisation. The real challenge is to lead effectively without formal authority and to harness influence from within the system. This form of leadership cultivates collaboration, fosters innovation, and empowers individuals to reach their full potential. When positioned without a high-ranking title, you can leverage unconventional strategies to undermine traditional hierarchies. By questioning assumptions and proposing alternative solutions, you can challenge thestatus quo. This approach may unsettle those in leadership, prompting them to engage with your ideas. title: Compliant but Unacceptable: Lessons for Colombo from Sydney and London About Built Form and Public Amenity
summary: BY DR SARATH MATARAARACHCHI As outlined in previous columns, over the past two to three decades, entrepreneurial urbanism has swept across the globe with remarkable momentum, transforming cities and creating urban environments of unprecedented scale and ambition. This has occurred as Government coffers diminished to meet infrastructure demands and as modern society became more sophisticated through technological advances and rising aspirations. There was a strong incentive for private capital to invest in urban development, since cities are increasingly regarded as engines of growth, centres of power and prosperity. Supported by vast pools of capital and strong institutions, this trend has delivered iconic buildings, transformative infrastructure, and carefully curated urban landscapes that project power, prosperity, and international relevance, often serving political elites, corporate interests, and international capital, all within broadly predictable planning frameworks. In much of the Global South, however, what has emerged is a diluted and distorted version of this model, best described as pseudo-entrepreneurial urbanism. Here, ambition is high but, institutional capacity is uneven, and the promise of urban renewal is pursued not through coherent planning, strong regulation, and public accountability, but through bending rules and opportunistic application of generic regulations to favour select development interests. title: US‑Israeli attack on Iran risks plunging the world into turmoil
summary: The US and Israel have launched extensive, coordinated attacks on numerous targets across Iran, prompting retaliatory strikes in the region. title: Forty years on, ‘honour’ still tries to silence women
summary: By Azra Syed Forty years ago, when I asked for my right to study, my family did not beat or kill me. Instead, they married me to the Quran — a symbolic punishment meant to end education without bloodshed. I was just 16 and continued to resist. My parents disowned me and sent me to live with my elder sister, who already had two young daughters and more responsibility than she could afford. They did not kill me. But they tried to kill my passion for education. That, too, is how ‘honour’ works. It does not always arrive with knives or ropes. Sometimes it comes quietly — through banishment, emotional exile, and the calculated narrowing of a woman’s future. Survival is permitted; ambition is not. And it is important to say this clearly. It was not culture, religion, or society that forced my parents’ hand, that shaped the fate of a Banaz Mahmod, or that authorised the sexual violence inflicted on a Mukhtar Mai. It was, and remains, a system. A system that encourages misogynistic and patriarchal societies by promoting a well-established and carefully managed propaganda: One that teaches families that control is duty, that punishment is protection, and that a woman’s autonomy is a threat to collective order. title: Sri Lanka’s Path to Strategic Sovereignty
summary: Sri Lanka’s future will be shaped not only by what the world does to us, but by how clearly we define and defend our own interests. In an era when every nation is effectively ‘for itself’, strategic sovereignty can no longer be an abstract slogan for Sri Lanka; it must become a deliberate national project. What strategic sovereignty means for a small State For a small state, strategic sovereignty is less about isolation and more about the capacity to make and implement independent choices in the shadow of larger powers. It is the ability to pursue national interests without becoming structurally dependent—economically, militarily, or technologically—on any single external actor. For Sri Lanka, this is complicated by geography and history. Sitting astride key Indian Ocean sea lanes, the island has long attracted interest from major powers, turning location into both an asset and a vulnerability. Small States typically balance two imperatives: influence and autonomy. They seek enough relevance in regional and global affairs to secure support and investment, while preserving the freedom to say “no” when core interests are threatened. This is the essential tension Sri Lanka must manage as India, China, the United States and others compete across the IndoPacific. title: The Ripple Effect of Workplace Microaggressions
summary: By Prasanna Perera Workplace microaggressions are subtle yet damaging forces that shape professional environments in overlooked ways. Unlike overt discrimination or severe harassment, these persistent acts of exclusion, bias and arrogance erode confidence and hinder careers. Examples include a raised eyebrow at a junior employee’s suggestion, comments about a colleague of colour being “surprisingly well-spoken,” or jokes about a working mother’s dual responsibilities. While companies tout diversity and inclusion, the true measure of a workplace culture lies in the unspoken messages conveyed through everyday interactions, which can create invisible barriers for those affected. The deceptive nature of microaggressions –Microaggressions in the workplace act as a subtle yet sinister force, gradually undermining morale, motivation, and mental well-being. Unlike overt acts of discrimination, these seemingly minor slights are often overlooked or dismissed, allowing their detrimental effects to accumulate over time. You may not immediately recognise the harm they inflict on your confidence and career advancement, but eventually, you could grapple with self-doubt, questioning your worth in an environment that should uplift you. Acknowledging these issues is essential to advocate for a more inclusive and supportive workplace culture. The gaslighting cycle –The underhanded nature of microaggressions often leads to their invalidation. When you express discomfort about subtle slights, you may encounter responses that make you question your own experiences, causing you to feel irrational about your feelings. Over time, this can lead to internalising the belief that your concerns are trivial, resulting in silence and suffering. title: Robust Domestic Consumption Is China’s New Economic Engine
summary: By Dr. Imran Khalid In the world of international economics, there are moments that serve as a testament to the sheer scale and potential of a nation’s internal engine. For China, that moment is the Spring Festival – the largest annual human migration on the planet. This year, the “Year of the Horse” has delivered far more than a seasonal surge in travel. It has provided a definitive look at a world power successfully navigating the most significant pivot in modern history: the transition to a high-quality, consumption-driven economy. If you look at the data flowing out of Beijing, the numbers are, by any measure, breathtaking. We are witnessing a record-breaking holiday period that has effectively redefined the Chinese consumer’s role in the global market. Official reports indicate that nearly 9.5 billion cross-regional trips will be completed by the end of this travel rush. To put that in perspective, that is the equivalent of the entire global population moving across a continent and back again. But the real story is not just the volume of people; it is the unprecedented flow of capital. Data from the Ministry of Commerce shows that during this extended nine-day break, average daily sales for major retail and dining enterprises rose by 8.6 per cent compared to last year. title: Rumesh Tharanga Wins Rome Diamond League with Record-Breaking 92.62m Throw
summary: Sri Lankan javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga delivered a historic performance at the Rome Diamond League, stunning the athletics world with a colossal throw of 92.62m. The effort not only secured his maiden Diamond League victory but also set a new national record, a meet record, and sealed the world lead once again. Just days after making his Diamond League debut in Rabat, where he finished second, Tharanga soared past the 90m mark for the first time in Rome , achieving the milestone on his second attempt. That throw sealed his place in history, making him the 8th best javelin thrower of all time. Remarkably, Tharanga now owns the first, second, third, and fifth best throws of 2026, cementing his status as the man to beat in javelin this season. Rising Star from Kalutara At just 23 years old, Tharanga’s journey from a schoolboy cricketer in Kalutara to global athletics stardom has been extraordinary. Initially a fast bowler clocking 134 km/h, he switched to throwing events under the guidance of his father, a former discus and shot-put athlete. By 2017, he had embraced the javelin, setting the stage for his meteoric rise. His early career included a 6th-place finish at the Asian Junior Championships in 2021 and a 7th-place finish at the World Junior Championships in 2022. After limited opportunities, he broke through with an 85.45m throw at the Asian Throwing Championships in South Korea, narrowly missing Olympic qualification. Fast forward to 2026, and Tharanga trained under Tony Prasanna is no longer an underdog. His 7th-place finish at the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo, ahead of Olympic champions Neeraj Chopra and Arshad Nadeem, confirmed his credentials as a rising force. Looking Ahead Following his triumph in Rome, Tharanga is set to continue on the Diamond League circuit, with appearances in Ostrava and Doha later this month. summary: Star javelin thrower Rumesh Tharangahas climbed to 5th place in the World Rankings following his impressive second-place finish in his Diamond League debut earlier this week. title: Kusal, Nissanka, bowlers put Sri Lanka 1-0 up
summary: Kusal Mendis struck a fluent 72 off 62 balls to energize Sri Lanka after a cautious start, while Pathum Nissanka, Janith Liyanage, and Charith Asalanka added crucial runs to lift the visitors to 303 for 7. Maheesh Theekshana delivered superb figures of 2 for 26, consistently deceiving batters with his variations, while Wanindu Hasaranga chipped in with 1 for 43. West Indies captain Shai Hope was the lone half-centurion, scoring 56 from 66 balls, but his side never managed to build a lasting partnership. title: Tharushi Abhisheka Strikes Gold at Asian Junior Athletics Championship
summary: Middle-distance runner Tharushi Abhisheka opened Sri Lanka’s medal account at the Asian Junior (U20) Athletics Championship in Hong Kong, winning the Gold Medal in the Women’s 1500m. The 18-year-old clocked 4:31.41 to outpace Iran’s Maryam Baluoutaki and South Korea’s Song Dawson, who finished second and third respectively. Nicknamed“Podi Tharushi”on the local track—after Olympian Tharushi Karunarathne—Abhisheka competes in both the 800m and 1500m events under the guidance of coach Buddhika Nuwan. She received her early education at Gampola Wickramabahu MMV before moving to Lyceum International School, Wattala.

title: Tuskers clinch historic CASA Sevens double
summary: The Sri Lanka men’s and women’s rugby sevens teams produced a stunning double victory to become the inaugural champions of the Central Asia and South Asia (CASA) Sevens Tournament in Uzbekistan last weekend. Led by skipper Srinath Sooriyabandara, the Sri Lanka men completed the tournament unbeaten and crushed India 31-10 in the final after already defeating the same opponents 33-12 in the preliminary round. At the same time, the Sri Lanka women, captained by Charani Liyanage, outclassed Kazakhstan 27-0 in a one-sided final to seal a memorable championship victory. The tournament featured six men’s and six women’s teams. Sri Lanka, India, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia fielded both men’s and women’s teams, while Pakistan competed only in the men’s category and Kazakhstan took part in the women’s event. Men’s squad included Srinath Sooriyabandara (captain), Janindu Dilshan (vice captain), Chathura Vidanalage, Akash Madusanka, Kavindu de Costa, Kavindu Perera, Ramith Himasha, Ravindu Anjula, Suranga Tennakoon, Diluksha Dange, Gayan Perera and Chemod Muthunayake, while Denuwan Wickramarachchi, Maliksha Perera and Jayathu Rajarathna were named as reserves. Women’s squad comprised Charani Liyanage (captain), Sanjeewani Wijetilake (vice captain), Hekashani Krishnakumari, Dilini Kanchana, Kaveesha Ishani Perera, Idusha Janani Perera, Priyanka Dilrukshi, Jayanthi Kumari Dilrukshi, Sanjeewani Perera, Nipuni Rasanjali, Dilki Sathsarani and Nirasha Dissanayake. The reserves were Sarani Nayanathara, Ruwanthi Tharushika and Nadeesha Dissanayake.

title: Ayatollah Khamenei’s iron grip on power in Iran comes to an end
summary: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has been killed on the first day of massive US and Israeli air strikes on Iran, US President Donald Trump has announced. The death of the 86-year-old ruler of the past three decades – one of the longest in the world – was later confirmed on Iranian State TV. Iran has had only two supreme leaders since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. It’s an all-powerful office – the supreme leader is Head of State and commander-in-chief of the armed forces, including the elite Revolutionary Guards. Khamenei is not quite a dictator, positioned in the middle of a complex web of competing power centres, able to veto any matter of public policy and hand pick candidates for public office. Young Iranians have never experienced life without him in charge. State television has covered Khamenei’s every move. summary: School holidays are precious, protected time for the Prince and Princess of Wales. Last week was half term. Prince William was back from his official visit to Saudi Arabia. summary: British comedian and actor Russell Brand ⁠has pleaded not guilty to two further charges of rape and sexual assault nearly ⁠two decades ago. Brand appeared at Southwark Crown ⁠Court in London on Tuesday and denied accusations of raping one woman and sexually assaulting a second woman in 2009. Once one of the United Kingdom’s most high-profile broadcasters, he was charged last year with two counts of rape, one count of indecent assault and two ‌counts of sexual assault against four women between 1999 and 2005. Brand pleaded not guilty in May last year to those five charges and is due to stand trial in June. A hearing will be held next month to decide whether the new allegations should be joined to that case, with Brand’s lawyer ⁠saying his client needs more time to address ⁠the latest offences. “These new charges are in relation to two further women and are in addition to the charges issued to Brand in April 2025, which involved four women,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement in December. Brand, 50, arrived at court wearing a white cowboy hat and sunglasses. Asked how he was feeling, the actor, who said in 2024 he had become ⁠a Christian, told reporters he was feeling “blessed”. Born in 1975 to working-class parents in Essex, east of London, Brand began his stand-up career as a teenager, eventually working as an MTV presenter and host of a reality TV series. A regular on British screens in the ⁠2000s, he was known for his flamboyant ⁠style and appearance. He also worked as a radio presenter for the BBC. Brand starred in several films, includingGet Him to the Greekin 2010, the year he married American pop star Katy Perry. They divorced in 2012 after 14 months of marriage. By the early 2020s, Brand had faded from and has since largely appeared online, airing his views on US politics and free speech. (Al-Jazeera)

title: India cuts dividend tax for large French investors
summary: India and France have revised a three-decade-old tax treaty, reducing dividend levies for large French investors while expanding Delhi’s powers to tax some transactions. The changes could benefit major companies such as Sanofi, Renault and L’Oreal, which have expanded their investments in India over the past few years. The agreement also gives Delhi the right to tax capital gains arising from the sale of shares, including transactions where a French entity owns less than 10% of an Indian company. The revised treaty also removes a most-favoured-nation (MFN) clause which had allowed French entities to claim a lower tax rate in India. It will come into effect after completing formalities and legal approvals in both countries. The details of the amended treaty were released by India’s Finance Ministry on Monday, days after French President Emmanuel Macron visited India. During the visit, the countries announced the elevation of their relationship to a “Special Global Strategic Partnership” and deepened cooperation in areas such as defence and space technology. In a joint statement on 17 February, they welcomed the amendment to the bilateral tax treaty. They said it would “secure economic activity for French and Indian businesses and pave the way for greater investments and collaborations between the two countries”. title: Violence erupts in Mexico after drug lord El Mencho killed
summary: A wave of violence has broken out in Mexico after the country’s most wanted drug baron was killed in an operation seeking his arrest. Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as “El Mencho”, was the leader of the feared Jalisco New Generation (CJNG) drug cartel and died after being seriously injured in clashes between his supporters and the Army on Sunday. Four CJNG members were killed during the operation in the town of Tapalpa, in the central-western Jalisco state, and three Army personnel were also injured, the Mexican Defence Ministry said. Retaliation for the drug lord’s death has seen violence spread to at least a dozen states, with CJNG blocking roads with burning vehicles. Throughout Sunday there were reports of gunmen on the streets in Jalisco and elsewhere. Eyewitnesses filmed plumes of smoke rising over several cities including Guadalajara – one of the host cities of the forthcoming Fifa World Cup. Jalisco’s Governor Pablo Lemus Navarro declared a code red in the state, pausing all public transport and cancelling mass events and in-person classes. Tourists who spoke to news agency Reuters described the resort town of Puerto Vallarta as a “war zone”. Some 250 roadblocks were in place across the country during the unrest, with 65 in Jalisco, the BBC’s US news partner CBS reported. In its latest update, the Mexican Security Cabinet said four blockades remained active in Jalisco. The Cabinet says 25 people have been arrested, 11 for their alleged participation in violent acts and 14 more for alleged looting and pillaging. Shops were on fire and about 20 bank branches were attacked in the violence, it added. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said there was “absolute co-ordination” between state and federal officials in response to the violence, urging people to stay “calm and informed”. title: Why Southasian diasporas are rejecting far-right politics
summary: By Inderjeet Parmar With 2026 already underway, the Southasian diaspora in the United States and United Kingdom stands at a pivotal crossroads. Rising far-right populism, economic anxieties, imperial overreach, and resurgent racism have placed these communities, once again, under intense pressure. Yet, far from succumbing to division or despair, the diaspora is increasingly contributing to broad, multiracial coalitions resisting authoritarianism, oligarchic capture, and elite dominance. The old chant “The people united will never be defeated”, resonates deeply. History repeatedly proves that when ordinary people overcome fear and manufactured divisions to stand together for justice and dignity, even the most entrenched powers falter. For Southasians in the U.S. and U.K., 2026 offers real prospects for hope, rooted in cross-community solidarity, anti-racist mobilisation, and a shared rejection of big-money rule. In the United States, the Southasian diaspora of over five million has faced a sharp escalation in hostility under Donald Trump’s second term. Hate incidents surged after the 2024 election – racial slurs increased by 66% while threats of violence went up by almost 60%, mostly against Southasians, according to the Stop AAPI Hate organisation. Far-right influencers scapegoated Indians over H-1B visas and tariffs, even turning on once-favoured figures like Vivek Ramaswamy. title: US shoots down Iranian drone approaching aircraft carrier, official says
summary: The U.S. military on Tuesday shot down an Iranian drone that “aggressively” approached the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea, the U.S. military said. The incident came as diplomats sought to arrange nuclear talks between Iran and the United States, and U.S. President Donald Trump warned that with U.S. warships heading toward Iran, “bad things” would probably happen if a deal could not be reached. Oil futures prices rose more than $1 per barrel after news the drone was shot down. The Iranian Shahed-139 drone was flying toward the carrier “with unclear intent” and was shot down by an F-35 U.S. fighter jet, the U.S. military said. “An F-35C fighter jet from Abraham Lincoln shot down the Iranian drone in self-defense and to protect the aircraft carrier and personnel on board,” said Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson at the U.S. military’s Central Command. Iran’s U.N. mission declined to comment. Iran’s Tasnim news agency said connection had been lost with a drone in international waters, but the reason was unknown. No American service members were harmed during the incident and no U.S. equipment was damaged, he added. The Lincoln carrier strike group is the most visible part of a U.S. military buildup in the Middle East following a violent crackdown against anti-government demonstrations last month, the deadliest domestic unrest in Iran since its 1979 revolution. Trump, who stopped short of carrying out threats to intervene during the crackdown, has since demanded Tehran make nuclear concessions and sent a flotilla to its coast. He said last week Iran was “seriously talking,” while Tehran’s top security official, Ali Larijani, said arrangements for negotiations were under way. (Reuters)

title: Unable or Unwilling? Indonesia’s Failed Natural Disaster Response
summary: By Adelina Kamal and John Bryant The floods and landslides that swept northern parts of Sumatra, Indonesia’s westernmost major island, at the end of November and persisted into December claimed more than 1,200 lives, and more than a hundred are still missing. They also displaced over a million people at the peak of the crisis, and devastated communities across multiple provinces. Entire villages disappeared or were submerged under mud and industrial debris, critical infrastructure collapsed, and livelihoods were wiped out. This was less the result of an isolated disaster than the cumulative consequence of long-term ecological destruction, disaster governance failures, and extractive development policies that have progressively stripped away natural protective systems and exposed communities to foreseeable risks. For many Indonesians concerned at the slow pace of the Government’s response, the debate has centred on whether the Sumatra floods should have been declared a national disaster, given the central government’s reluctance to do so. title: Bitcoin nears $100,000 as investors bet on crypto-friendly Trump policies
summary: Bitcoin is nearing the $100,000 mark as crypto enthusiasts bet that United States President-elect Donald Trump will usher in a more welcoming regulatory environment for digital assets. The world’s most popular digital currency rose as high as $99,073 on Thursday, extending its surge since Trump’s re-election on November 5. The commodity has risen more than 60 percent since election day as investors anticipate Trump’s incoming administration to ease regulatory and legal hurdles to its use. Trump, who called the asset a “scam” during his first term, accepted campaign donations in cryptocurrency, and has pledged to make the US “the crypto capital of the planet” and accumulate a national bitcoin reserve. Trump and his three sons in September also announced the launch of their own crypto business, World Liberty Financial, which investors have taken as a promising sign of the president-elect’s belief in the sector. In another bullish signal for the sector on Thursday, United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chair, Gary Gensler, who was widely disliked among crypto investors for his aggressive enforcement actions targeting the sector, confirmed that he would step down in January. Trump had pledged to fire Gensler on “day one” of his administration, though the president does not have the authority to remove the SEC chair before the end of his or her term. While viewed by supporters as a ticket to big returns and financial freedom, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are known for their volatility and have faced government crackdowns in several parts of the world. After climbing to a record high of $69,000 in late 2021, Bitcoin plunged to less than $16,000 over the following year. The commodity burst past its previous peak in March after gaining more than 300 percent since November 2022.

title: Universal Merit Awards 2024 will be held at BMICH, Colombo: Mahinda Rajapaksa will be the chief guest, Bollywood director Dushyant will direct
summary: India’s Allso Group is organizing the Universal Merit Awards 2024 at the BMICH International Convention Center in Colombo, the capital of Sri Lanka, on 7 August 2024. title: Rathupaswala shooting: all accused army personnel acquitted
summary: The four accused army personnel in the case of Rathupaswala shooting in 2013 in which three including a school student were killed and nearly 50 persons were injured, were acquitted by the Trial-at-Bar at Gampaha High Court. Delivering the verdict today (17), the court ordered to acquit the four Sri Lanka army personnel including a Major General and three soldiers as the Attorney General has failed to prove the guilt beyond reasonable doubt. On 1 August 2013, army personnel opened fire at unarmed villagers at Weliweriya, killing three and injuring about 50 persons, as they protested against a factory which they said polluted their groundwater and demanded clean drinking water. In August 2019, then Chief Justice Jayantha Jayasuriya appointed a Trial-at-Bar consisting High Court Judges Menaka Wijesundara (President), Nimal Ranaweera and Nishantha Hapuarachchi to hear the Rathupaswala case, after considering the Attorney General’s request. On 11 September 2019, the Attorney General filed indictments before the Trial-at-Bar at the Gampaha High Court, against then-Brigadier Anura Deshapriya Gunawardena and 3 other military persons for allegedly ordering troops to open fire on protesters demanding clean water in Rathupaswala in 2013. On April 30, 2024, the Gampaha High Court’s Trial-at-Bar deferred delivering the verdict in the case until today (17).

title: Public Notice: NSB addresses misinterpretation amidst SLSB acquisition
summary: The National Savings Bank (NSB) has issued a clarification regarding a misinterpretation on National Savings Bank (NSB), amongst the public, of a news item, currently circulating pertaining to the the Sri Lanka Savings Bank (SLSB). In a statement issued today (15), the NSB said, “We wish to clarify that SLSB is a fully owned subsidiary of NSB, and that the recent developments involve the proposed acquisition of SLSB with NSB, pursuant to a regulatory directive by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL). Further, the information in circulation regarding a Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) and the termination of operations are solely related to the SLSB and not applicable to NSB. We wish to emphasise that this decision does not have any impact on the stability of NSB. We expect that this clarification addresses any confusion and wish to assure the continued strength and integrity of National Savings Bank.”

title: Ceyline Holdings appoints new Dy. Chairman and Group Director
summary: Ceyline Holdings (Pvt) Ltd. During his naval career, he was awarded the Vishishta Seva Vibhushanaya (VSV) and Uttama Seva Padakkama (USP) for exemplary conduct in recognition of the service rendered by him to the motherland. Admiral De Silva was conferred with the Golden Award for Professional Excellence in the Maritime and Defence Category at the 2022 National APEX awards ceremony. title: Elephant House Dominates at SLIM Brand Excellence 2023!
summary: Elephant House dazzled once again as a brand powerhouse by securing 3 prestigious awards at the SLIM Brand Excellence Awards 2023. Hosted by the Sri Lanka Institute of Marketing, Brand Excellence is the most prestigious recognition for brands in Sri Lanka, honoring exceptional marketing efforts and outstanding brand stories. Elephant House Ice Cream won Gold in Product Brand of the Year, dominating in a competitive category contested by the strongest FMCG brands, local and multinational. Elephant House Ice Cream also won Silver in Local Brand of the Year, an extremely competitive category contested by the top brands in Sri Lanka. The brand’s strategies and actions to connect with consumers as “Sri Lanka’s Favorite Ice Cream” in a challenging year was duly recognized by the jury with these awards. Gunadamin Elephant House won Bronze in CSR Brand of the Year. Gunadamin Elephant House operates for the greater good of society through Community upliftment, Waste management and Sustainable sourcing. The brand activities in this end were recognized and rewarded by the jury through this prestigious award. “These awards solidify the power of Elephant House as a brand loved and trusted by generations of Sri Lankans. We are committed to connect with our consumers by creating joyful and exciting moments in their everyday lives.” Expressed DamindaGamlath, President of the Consumer Foods Sector – John Keells Holdings PLC, speaking of the victories achieved by the brand. These awards add to the many accolades received by the brand this year, validating the positioning of Elephant House in the hearts of Sri Lankans.
